cards.text: Saul is dead (1 Samuel 31:6), and now there are TWO kings. The men of Judah anointed David king in Hebron, and Abner son of Ner, commander of Saul's army, made Saul's son Ish-bosheth king over Israel (2 Samuel 2:4, 8-9). One day Abner and the servants of Ish-bosheth march out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.

cards.question: Abner's side is headed for Gibeon. Who marches out with David's servants to meet them?

cards.text: The two groups take up positions on opposite sides of the pool of Gibeon, like two drivers nose to nose on a one-lane bridge. Then Abner speaks up to Joab.

cards.question: Abner looks across the pool at Joab and makes a suggestion. What is it?

answers.text: Let the young men compete before them
Let the two kings meet and talk
Let both sides go home in peace

cards.question: Joab turns down Abner's idea.
The young men at the pool of Gibeon get up and are counted off, ___ on each side.

cards.text: The contest starts. Each man grabs his opponent by the head and thrusts his sword into his opponent's side, all twenty-four of them.

cards.question: When every young man at Gibeon strikes his opponent's side, one side clearly wins the contest.

cards.text: They all fall together. That place in Gibeon gets a name: Helkath-hazzurim.

cards.question: After the contest at the pool, the battle that day is intense. Who ends up defeated?

answers.text: Abner and the men of Israel
Joab and the servants of David
The Philistines who join the fight

cards.text: The three sons of Zeruiah are there: Joab, Abishai and Asahel, and Asahel is fleet of foot like a wild gazelle. Me, I'm on a gold base, friend, so my top speed is HOP.

cards.question: In the middle of the battle, speedy Asahel takes off running after ___.
Asahel chases Abner without turning to the right or to the left.

cards.text: With Asahel on his heels, Abner glances back and STILL checks caller ID: “Is that you, Asahel?” Asahel says it is.

cards.question: Abner tells Asahel to turn to his right or his left. What does he tell him to do instead of chasing him?

answers.text: Grab one of the young men and take his gear
Go back and wait with his brother Joab
Drop his weapons and head home to Hebron

cards.question: Asahel takes Abner's advice and stops chasing him.

cards.text: So Abner warns him a second time: “Stop chasing me. Why should I strike you to the ground?”

cards.question: Abner adds one more question to his warning. Who does he say he couldn't show his face to if he struck Asahel down?

cards.text: But Asahel refuses to turn away. So Abner thrusts the butt of his spear into his stomach, it comes out his back, and Asahel falls dead on the spot.

cards.question: Asahel has fallen and died on the battlefield. What does every man do when he comes to the place where Asahel fell?

cards.text: Asahel is gone, but his brothers Joab and Abishai keep after Abner. By sunset they've come as far as the hill of Ammah, on the way to the wilderness of Gibeon.

cards.question: Joab and Abishai are closing in on Abner at sunset. What do the Benjamites with Abner do?

answers.text: Rally to Abner and take a stand on a hill
Scatter and run off in every direction
Hand Abner over to Joab and Abishai

cards.text: Then Abner calls down from the hill to Joab: “Must the sword devour forever? Do you not realize that this will only end in bitterness?”

cards.question: Abner asks Joab how long it'll be before he does something. What does Abner want Joab to do?

answers.text: Tell the troops to stop chasing their brothers
Meet him alone on top of the hill
Bring King David out to talk with him

cards.question: Joab answers Abner's plea. What does Joab say would have happened if Abner hadn't spoken up?

answers.text: The troops would have kept chasing until morning
The troops would have stopped at sunset anyway
The troops would have surrounded the hill

cards.question: Joab blows the ram's horn, and his troops charge up the hill after Abner.

cards.text: All the troops stop, and the fighting is over. Then all that night Abner and his men march through the Arabah and cross the Jordan.

cards.question: After marching all morning, Abner and his men arrive back at ___.
Joab comes back from chasing Abner and gathers all his troops. How do the two sides' losses compare?

answers.text: David's side lost far fewer men
Both sides lost about the same
Abner's side lost far fewer men

cards.text: Besides Asahel, nineteen of David's servants are missing. But they struck down 360 Benjamites who were with Abner.

cards.question: David's men take Asahel and bury him in his father's tomb in ___.

cards.text: Then Joab and his men march all night and reach Hebron at daybreak. Two armies, two all-nighters, and the last all-nighter I pulled was counting dust in the back of that junk drawer, and I LOST COUNT.

cards.question: After Gibeon, the war between the house of Saul and the house of David drags on for a long time.
As the war between Saul's house and David's house goes on, what happens to the two sides?

answers.text: David grows stronger and Saul's house grows weaker
Saul's house grows stronger and David grows weaker
Both sides keep growing weaker and weaker

cards.text: Back in Hebron, six sons are born to David, each by a different mother. His firstborn is Amnon, by Ahinoam of Jezreel, and his third is Absalom, son of Maacah daughter of King Talmai of Geshur.
And that's where we leave it for now, friend. The oven timer on this story hasn't even gone off yet.
